net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
The Company’s revenue recognition policy is based on the revenue recognition criteria established under the Financial Accounting Standards Board – Accounting Standards Codification 606 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers ” which has established a five-step process to govern contract revenue and satisfy each element is as follows:

(1) Identify the contract(s) with a customer.

(2) identify the performance obligations in the contract.

(4) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and

(5) recognize revenue when or as you satisfy a performance obligation.

The Company records the revenue once all the above steps are completed.

A performance obligation is a promise in a contract to transfer a distinct good or service to the customer and is the unit of account in the contract. A contract’s transaction price is allocated to each distinct performance obligation and recognized as revenue when, or as, the performance obligation is satisfied.

The Company recognizes revenues from card sales when the product is deemed delivered to the customer, and the ownership/control is transferred.

net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
The Company’s revenue recognition policy is based on the revenue recognition criteria established under the Financial Accounting Standards Board – Accounting Standards Codification 606 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers ” which has established a five-step process to govern contract revenue and satisfy each element is as follows:

(1) Identify the contract(s) with a customer.

(2) identify the performance obligations in the contract.

(4) allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and

(5) recognize revenue when or as you satisfy a performance obligation.

The Company records the revenue once all the above steps are completed.

A performance obligation is a promise in a contract to transfer a distinct good or service to the customer and is the unit of account in the contract. A contract’s transaction price is allocated to each distinct performance obligation and recognized as revenue when, or as, the performance obligation is satisfied.

The Company’s parent recognizes revenues from card sales when the product is deemed delivered to the customer, and the ownership/control is transferred. lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Our future success depends upon the active and effective promotion of our products and services by retail distributors, but their interests and operational decisions might not always align with our interests.

Due to the fact that most of our revenues will be derived from commissions from the sale of our products and services, future revenue growth depends on our ability to retain and attract new long-term users of the products.
Our future success depends on our ability to attract, integrate, retain and incentivize key personnel.

The trading price of our Common Stock depends on a number of factors, including those described in this “Risk Factors” section, many of which are beyond our control and may not be related to our operating performance.

The payment of dividends on Common Stock will depend on earnings, financial condition and other business and economic factors affecting it at such times as the board of directors may consider relevant.

The declaration of any future cash dividends is at the discretion of our board of directors and depends upon our earnings, if any, our capital requirements and financial position, our general economic conditions, and other pertinent conditions.
Our capital requirements for the next fiscal year will depend on numerous factors, including management’s evaluation of the timing of projects to pursue.
The Company does not rely on pre- approval policies and procedures.
